correctness.rationale: For any set X of worlds, the Diamond-image tests intersection with the union of the atom supports of X. In the definable tail [k,n], the minimum-parity color opposite to k never uses atom k and contains the entire world [k+1,n]. Its Diamond-image, negated and intersected with the tail, therefore isolates precisely the world {k}; applying Diamond again gives membership of atom k in any world. Excluding that coordinate produces the next tail. At k=n the tail already isolates its only world. The coordinate tests exhaustively distinguish worlds, and finite unions give all propositions. Both constants are fixed by Diamond, so no zero-generator modal algebra is full when n≥2; at n=1 the constants suffice. The pure Boolean lower bound is 2^r≥2^n−1 and the n coordinate generators attain it. The argument is for Boolean complement on sets of worlds and unrestricted valuations. Finite bit-mask and partition-refinement evidence was inspected, not rerun; the induction supplies all orders.
